title: In Ephesians 1 What Does It Mean To Be Chosen By God Before The Foundation Of The World
paragraphs: Exploring God's Choice: "Chosen Before the Foundation of the World" in Ephesians 1

One of the most profound and awe-inspiring passages in the New Testament is found in Ephesians 1. The apostle Paul, writing to believers in Ephesus, opens his letter with a sweeping vision of God's eternal plan for salvation. Central to this vision is the statement that believers are "chosen" by God "before the foundation of the world." What does this mean? How should we understand this biblical doctrine?
The Text in Focus
even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blemish before him in love: - Ephesians 1:4 ASV

Paul declares that God’s choice of believers was not an afterthought or a reaction to human events, but an expression of His eternal purpose—made "before the foundation of the world." This phrase emphasizes God’s sovereignty and the initiative He takes in salvation.
God’s Initiative in Salvation
The Bible consistently teaches that our salvation is not based on human merit, but on God's gracious initiative. This is highlighted again in Ephesians 1:
having foreordained us unto adoption as sons through Jesus Christ unto himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, - Ephesians 1:5 ASV
God’s choice is described as being “according to the good pleasure of his will.” Salvation is rooted in God’s character and purpose, not in anything we have done.
What Does It Mean to Be "Chosen"?

To be "chosen" (Greek: eklegomai) means to be selected or set apart for a purpose. In the context of Ephesians 1, believers are chosen “in him”—that is, in Christ. This choosing is not arbitrary or impersonal, but relational and Christ-centered.
Chosen for Holiness: The goal of God’s choice is that believers “should be holy and without blemish before him.” God’s election leads to transformation and sanctification (1 Peter 1:15).
Chosen for Adoption: God’s purpose is to adopt us as His children through Jesus Christ, bringing us into His family (Galatians 4:4-5).
God’s Sovereignty and Human Response
While God’s sovereign choice is clear, the Bible also teaches that individuals must respond to God’s grace through faith. Paul elsewhere emphasizes:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man should glory. - Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV

This means that although God initiates salvation and draws people to Himself (John 6:44), we are called to respond in faith. The tension between God's sovereignty and human responsibility has been widely discussed among believers, but the clear teaching is that salvation is entirely by grace, received through faith.
The Assurance and Purpose of Being Chosen

Knowing we are chosen by God brings profound assurance and security. Our salvation rests on God’s eternal purpose, not on our fluctuating feelings or performance. This truth is meant to lead us to praise and worship:
to the end that we should be unto the praise of his glory, we who had before hoped in Christ: - Ephesians 1:12 ASV
Being chosen is not a reason for pride but for humble gratitude, leading us to live holy lives for God’s glory.
Different Perspectives on Election

Some Christians interpret “chosen before the foundation of the world” as indicating that God sovereignly elects certain individuals for salvation (the doctrine of unconditional election). Others emphasize that God’s choice is based on His foreknowledge of who would believe (conditional election). While perspectives vary, all agree that salvation is by God's grace through faith in Christ.
Conclusion

To be "chosen by God before the foundation of the world" means that God, in His infinite wisdom and love, purposed to save and transform those who would trust in Christ. It is a truth that should fill us with awe, humility, and a desire to live for His glory.
